newsitem.title: JAPAN: No decision on extra budget for Japan economy - MOF.
newsitem.headline: No decision on extra budget for Japan economy - MOF.

text.p: Japan's government has not made any "positive decision" towards drafting a large scale extra budget for the sake of the economy, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo told reporters on Tuesday.

Kubo denied a Sunday report in the Nihon Keizai Shimbun that said the government may come with a supplementary budget after the general election which is expected to be called in October and accelerate implementation of public works projects worth one trillion yen to be allocated under next year's budget.

Asked about the report, Kubo said: "I know nothing about that. It seems that the likely amount of public spending in the latter half of this fiscal year could be the same as the amount seen in the latter half of last fiscal year."
Kubo also said his ministry's project team is likely to come up with its own reform plans in the not too distant future.
